survey: Image 4 shows a sci-fi control console: a box-shaped grey cabinet on a riveted metal-tile floor. The camera is high, in front and slightly to the right. 1) Cabinet body: the front face is nearly square to the camera, with vertical edges kept vertical. Its top and bottom edges drop slightly toward the right and converge gently to the left, which fits a viewpoint above the object. A thin strip of the right side face shows, which fits a vanishing point just past the right edge. 2) Drawer: an inset panel with a horizontal handle. Its edges run parallel to the front face's edges. 3) Slanted top panel: it slopes from a raised back rail down to the front edge and is seen from above. Its left and right edges lean inward toward the back, in the same direction as the cabinet's back-to-front edges. The back rail is shorter than the front edge, as perspective would make it. 4) Two gauges: round dials lying on the slanted panel, drawn as ellipses flattened by about the same amount as the panel's tilt. 5) Eight buttons in two staggered rows: the rows slope with the panel's front edge, the buttons are drawn as matching ellipses, and the front row is slightly larger than the back row. 6) Joystick: a raised slot block sits flat on the panel, and its top face is seen from above like the panel. The lever rises straight up and ends in a red ball. 7) Contact with the floor: the cabinet's bottom edge sits flat on the tiled floor. The tile seams near the cabinet run roughly along its front edge and its back-to-front direction, and they are seen from the same high viewpoint.
